'''Paul Murray Bellan''' is a Canadian-American physicist. He is a professor of Applied Physics at [[Caltech]], working in experimental [[plasma physics]], [[magnetohydrodynamics]], and laboratory astrophysics. He is the author of the textbook ''Fundamentals of Plasma Physics''.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Bellan |first=Paul Murray |title=Fundamentals of plasma physics |date=2006 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-82116-2 |location=Cambridge}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Paul Bellan grew up in [[Winnipeg]], Canada. He earned a Bachelor of Science with honors in 1970 from the [[University of Manitoba]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web |last1=Zierler |first1=David |title=Paul M. Bellan, Plasma Physicist |url=https://heritageproject.caltech.edu/interviews-updates/paul-bellan |website=Heritage Project |publisher=California Institute of Technology |access-date=3 March 2025 |language=en |date=12 July 2022}}</ref> He went on to pursue his graduate studies in plasma physics at Princeton University, where he married fellow physicist [[Josette Bellan]]. He earned his Master of Arts in 1972 and his Ph.D. in 1976. His doctoral research, under the guidance of [[Miklos Porkolab]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Graduate Theses {{!}} Princeton Program in Plasma Physics |url=https://plasma.princeton.edu/education/graduate-theses |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=plasma.princeton.edu |language=en}}</ref> focused on the generation and behavior of lower hybrid waves generated by periodic antennae.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Bellan |first=Paul Murray |url=https://catalog.princeton.edu/catalog/999574683506421 |title=Theoretical and experimental studies of the propagation of electrostatic lower hybrid waves |date=1976}}</ref>

== Career ==
Prof. Bellan has served as faculty of the department of Applied Physics and Materials Science at Caltech since 1977, initially working closely with physicist [[Roy W. Gould]].<ref name=":0" /> He has mentored over 30 graduate students,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bellan Plasma Group at Caltech |url=http://bellanplasmagroup.caltech.edu/people/index.html |access-date=2025-07-02 |website=bellanplasmagroup.caltech.edu}}</ref> and has taught an introductory course on plasma physics, based on which he authored the textbook ''Fundamentals of Plasma Physics''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Montgomery |first=David C. |date=2007-01-01 |title=Paul M. Bellan (2006) Fundamentals of plasma physics |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s00162-006-0038-6 |journal=Theoretical and Computational Fluid Dynamics |language=en |volume=21 |issue=1 |pages=79–80 |doi=10.1007/s00162-006-0038-6 |issn=1432-2250|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Bellan’s research focuses on [[plasma physics]] through laboratory experiments, analytical models, and numerical simulations. He has contributed to plasma self-organization through [[Taylor state]] relaxation, especially [[Spheromak|in Spheromak]] formation, pioneering experimental work on Spheromak injection for noninductive [[Tokamak]] ramp-up. He has authored two graduate-level books on Spheromaks and [[Magnetic helicity]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Bellan |first=Paul Murray |title=Spheromaks: a practical application of magnetohydrodynamic dynamos and plasma self-organization |date=2000 |publisher=Imperial College Press |others=World Scientific (Firm) |isbn=978-1-86094-141-2 |location=London}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Bellan |first=Paul Murray |title=Magnetic helicity, spheromaks, solar Corona loops, and astrophysical jets |date=2018 |publisher=World Scientific |isbn=978-1-78634-516-5 |location=New Jersey London Singapore [und 6 weitere]}}</ref> He has also contributed to plasma laboratory astrophysics, performing experiments that model [[astrophysical jets]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Redefining Physics: Plasma Jets With Unexpected X-Ray Emissions |url=https://scitechdaily.com/redefining-physics-plasma-jets-with-unexpected-x-ray-emissions/ |work=SciTechDaily |date=22 December 2023}} [[solar prominences]],</ref> generation of [[nanoflare]]s by solar [[coronal loop]]s,<ref>{{cite news |title=Laboratory Solar Flares Reveal Clues to Mechanism Behind Bursts of High-Energy Particles |url=https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/laboratory-solar-flares-reveal-clues-to-mechanism-behind-bursts-of-high-energy-particles |publisher=California Institute of Technology |date=6 April 2023 |language=en}}</ref> and [[dusty plasma]] phenomena in [[Mesospheric cloud|noctilucent clouds]] and [[protoplanetary disk]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bellan |first=P. M. |date=2008 |title=Ice iron/sodium film as cause for high noctilucent cloud radar reflectivity |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1029/2008JD009927 |journal=Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres |language=en |volume=113 |issue=D16 |doi=10.1029/2008JD009927 |bibcode=2008JGRD..11316215B |issn=2156-2202}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Nicolov |first1=André |last2=Gudipati |first2=Murthy S. |last3=Bellan |first3=Paul M. |date=2024-05-01 |title=Phase and Morphology of Water-ice Grains Formed in a Cryogenic Laboratory Plasma |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |volume=966 |issue=1 |pages=66 |doi=10.3847/1538-4357/ad34b5 |doi-access=free |arxiv=2404.16396 |bibcode=2024ApJ...966...66N |issn=0004-637X}}</ref>

Bellan was elected a Fellow of the American Physical Society (APS) in 1991, and was awarded the Writing Award from the American Astronomical Society in 2001 for his article on solar prominences.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Physicists Honored by APS |journal=Physics Today |date=1 December 2001 |volume=54 |issue=12 |pages=68–69 |doi=10.1063/1.1445559 |bibcode=2001PhT....54S..68. |url=https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1445559 |issn=0031-9228}}</ref>
